items.q: All three families share what primitive?

blocks.label: detect (LC141) + find start (LC142)
blocks.py:
slow = fast = head
while fast and fast.next:
    slow = slow.next
    fast = fast.next.next
    if slow == fast:                 # CYCLE confirmed
        slow = head                  # reset one to head
        while slow != fast:          # walk BOTH 1-step
            slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next
        return slow                  # cycle ENTRY node

blocks.md: **Why start-finder works (say it verbatim):** meeting point is k steps into ring where k = distance from head-to-entry; walking both at speed 1 re-synchronizes exactly at entry. Proof lives in modular arithmetic — offer it if pushed.

blocks.label: merge two sorted lists (LC21) — dummy pattern
blocks.py:
dummy = Node(0); tail = dummy
while l1 and l2:
    if l1.val <= l2.val: tail.next, l1 = l1, l1.next
    else:                tail.next, l2 = l2, l2.next
    tail = tail.next
tail.next = l1 or l2                 # drain leftover
return dummy.next

blocks.md: **Dummy-head pattern deletes ALL special cases — tail always exists, return dummy->next. Use it in every construction problem from now on.**
